record.original_question: Does every holomorphic map F : P^k → P^k of degree at least two have a repelling periodic point? Do meromorphic maps have periodic orbits? -sibony@anh.matups.fr

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3.2 Does every holomorphic map F : Pk → Pk of degree at least two have a repelling periodic point? Do meromorphic maps have periodic orbits? -sibony@anh.matups.fr

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 1$ and let $\mathbb{P}^k$ denote complex projective space of dimension $k$. 

(a) Let $F : \mathbb{P}^k \to \mathbb{P}^k$ be a holomorphic map of algebraic degree $d \geq 2$. A periodic point $p$ of period $n$ (so $F^n(p)=p$) is called repelling if every eigenvalue of the derivative $DF^n(p)$ has modulus strictly greater than $1$. Must $F$ admit at least one repelling periodic point?

(b) Let $F : \mathbb{P}^k \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^k$ be a meromorphic (rational) self-map of $\mathbb{P}^k$. Must $F$ admit a periodic orbit, i.e., a point $p$ outside the indeterminacy set such that $F^n(p) = p$ for some $n \geq 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Briend and Duval (Acta Math. 182, 1999) proved that for any holomorphic endomorphism of P^k of degree d ≥ 2, repelling periodic points are not only existent but are equidistributed with respect to the equilibrium measure and dense in the Julia set, fully resolving part (a). The meromorphic/rational case (b) is more subtle: positive results exist under additional assumptions (e.g., algebraically stable maps with suitable dynamical degrees, work of Diller–Jackson–Sommese, Dinh–Sibony, and others) but the general existence-of-periodic-orbits question for arbitrary meromorphic self-maps of P^k does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Large entropy measures for endomorphisms of CP^k
status_evidence.snippet: Briend and Duval showed that the equilibrium measure is the limit of normalized sums of Dirac masses on repelling periodic points.
status_evidence.claim: Part (a) is resolved: holomorphic endomorphisms of P^k of degree ≥ 2 have (densely many) repelling periodic points.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium States of Endomorphisms of P^k
status_evidence.snippet: For holomorphic endomorphisms of P^k, repelling periodic points of period n are equidistributed with respect to the equilibrium state as n goes to infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Equidistribution of repelling periodic points confirmed for holomorphic endomorphisms of P^k.
